android_mechanism: Progress broadcast emitted on every change; fix reports only meaningful updates
bug_description: WebPage's onProgressChange handler writes a hilog log line for every progress event. Web progress fires dozens of times per page load (per sub-resource), so opening any article emits a log storm on the UI thread (formatting + hilog IPC per event), adding overhead to every page load.
fix_summary: Progress is logged only at milestones (every 25% and completion), cutting per-event formatting and hilog traffic during page loads.

test_oracle.definition: raw-instruction-retired sample count attributed to the app process during the measured step, aggregated from perf.data (HapRay perf.db instruction counts).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.measured_as: perf_hw-instructions over the web progress-callback window (Pura 70 Ultra)
evidence.note: 4.42M vs 3.52M median hw-instructions (1.26x, disjoint ranges); mechanism counter 101 vs 5 hilog calls per page load (measurements-staging).

mechanism_oracle.definition: Count of hilog invocations from the app during page load (progress-event logs), and UI-thread CPU from tap to page-end.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed logs on every progress event (dozens per page); fixed logs <= 5 per page. unfixed page-load UI CPU > fixed.

reproduction: git -C hosts/wanharmony checkout case/wanharmony_web_progress_log_storm/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/wanharmony checkout case/wanharmony_web_progress_log_storm/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
